title: Electric field at A
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the electric field strength at point A using E = F/q, yielding 4/3 N/C or approximately 1.33 N/C.

title: Force at B
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the magnitude of the electric force on q at point B, recognizing it is 1/4 of the force at A, yielding 1e-4 N.

title: Resultant field magnitude
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the magnitude of the resultant electric field at A from both Q and Q', yielding 8/3 N/C or approximately 2.67 N/C.

title: Resultant field direction
description: Important: Correctly states the direction of the resultant electric field at point A is from A to B (or equivalent, e.g., towards B).

title: Field-force relationship
description: Important: Applies the definition of electric field (E = F/q) to solve part (1) without incorrectly invoking Coulomb's law directly.

title: Inverse-square reasoning
description: Important: Recognizes that the force at B is 1/4 of the force at A due to the inverse-square law (distance doubled, force quartered).

title: Superposition principle
description: Important: Applies the principle of superposition to add the electric field vectors at A from Q and Q' for part (3).

title: Sign/direction confusion
description: Pitfall: Incorrectly assigns direction for the resultant field (e.g., from B to A) or confuses the effect of the opposite sign charge Q'.

title: Incorrect force scaling
description: Pitfall: Fails to correctly scale the force for part (2) (e.g., uses 1/2 instead of 1/4, or incorrectly uses E = F/q again).
